newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Another South Korean steel maker collapses.
newsitem.headline: Another South Korean steel maker collapses.

text.p: South Korea's biggest specialty steel products maker has filed for court receivership, company officials said on Wednesday.
It was the second steel company to collapse this year.

Sammi Steel Co and four affiliates sought protection from creditors on Tuesday. At the end of 1996 the steel firm's liabilities were 1.45 trillion won ($1.6 billion) against assets of 1.53 trillion won, according to company figures.

In January, Hanbo Steel Co filed for receivership under debts of $5.8 billion in the country's biggest corporate collapse. Hanbo is South Korea's second largest steelmaker after Pohang Iron and Steel Co.
Trading in shares of Sammi Steel and Sammi Corp were halted on the Seoul stock exchange and the shock sent the leading index lower soon after the opening.
Sammi Metal Products Co, Sammi Technology and Industries Co and Sammi Fine Ceramics Co -- other troubled units of Sammi Group -- are not listed.
Sammi Steel, buffeted by weak steel prices and staggering under the burden of debt repayment, posted a net loss of 119.98 billion won in calendar 1996 against a loss of 39.45 billion in 1995.
